source.citation: Kulik, D. A. (2002). Gibbs energy minimization approach to modeling sorption equilibria at the mineral-water interface: Thermodynamic relations for multi-site-surface complexation. American Journal of Science 302, 227-279.

transcription.note: The site densities were in src/surfaces/host_coupling.jl and the two shifts in test/site_families.jl before this file existed; all agree with the article. The minus signs of the two shifts are a special glyph that text extraction drops; they are read from the page and from the logarithms they print.

reference_site_density_nm2.description: Conventional reference total site density, in sites per nm^2, proposed as 2e-5 mol/m^2 for every surface species and every sorbent: the standard state of a monodentate surface species.

reference_site_density.description: The same reference density in the form Kulik proposes it; the value in nm^-2 is its rounded reading.

dzombak_morel_weak_site_density_nm2.description: Total site density, in sites per nm^2, at which Dzombak and Morel (1990) fitted their intrinsic constants of the weak sites of hydrous ferric oxide, as reported by Kulik.

dzombak_morel_strong_site_density_nm2.description: The same for the strong sites.

logk_shift_weak.description: The term Kulik adds to a weak-site intrinsic constant of Dzombak and Morel to refer it to the reference density, log(2.254/12.05), as printed (two decimals).

logk_shift_strong.description: The same for the strong sites, log(0.056/12.05).

notes: Equation (21), p. 250, converts an intrinsic constant fitted at a site density to the reference one; convert_logk_site_density implements it.
